clinician.final_diagnosis: Neurofibromatosis type 1 (NF1) confirmed by genetic testing showing a pathogenic variant of the NF1 gene
clinician.trajectory_summary: A 56-year-old man with a 28-year history of clinically diagnosed NF1 presented with recurrent spontaneous pneumothorax, prompting referral with suspicion for Birt-Hogg-Dubé syndrome. Physical examination on admission confirmed classic NF1 stigmata including multiple café-au-lait macules, axillary and groin freckling, multiple cutaneous and plexiform neurofibromas, and tongue fibromas. Chest X-ray documented a left apical pneumothorax (2006). High-resolution CT subsequently demonstrated bilateral lung bullae and apical cysts, leading to thoracic surgery referral; however, surgical intervention was deferred due to diffuse cyst localization and a 10-year interval since the prior pneumothorax episode. Family history confirmed NF1 in both mother and sister. The diagnosis of NF1 was genetically confirmed, establishing it as the unifying diagnosis accounting for the pulmonary cystic manifestations and distinguishing it from Birt-Hogg-Dubé syndrome.

Thoracic surgery consultation determined conservative management appropriate due to diffuse cyst localization and 10-year disease-free interval
